Subject: Temporal archival escape hatch - need confirmation

Hi Aditya,

We're finalizing a migration of logs to our custodian subprocessor and need clarity on Redwood's ability to support a short-term "bridge" for logs and snapshots during the handoff. Our security team asks:

- Can Redwood hold KV logs and incremental snapshots for up to 30 days in a transient buffer while we validate transfer integrity?
- If so, what controls/audit evidence will you provide (audit trail, attestations, access logs)?
- Will this require a DPA addendum or subprocessor attestation?

We've attached our DPA questions and a short migration checklist. Timing: we aim to start the transfer 2027-11-08 and would need the buffer window to begin 2027-11-08 and close no later than 2027-12-08.

Please advise next steps and whom we should loop on your side.

Thanks,
Sara Patel
Head of Security Operations
MediFlow

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear checklist.

Short answer: yes, we can support a short-lived bridge for logs and snapshots, but it requires a narrow DPA addendum and operational constraints. Proposed plan below (high level):

1) Transient buffer: up to 21 days by default; we can extend to 30 days by exception with legal sign-off.
2) Scope: immutable snapshots + KV cache segments used for request replay and forensic validation. Individual user payloads are not duplicated beyond normal backups.
3) Controls: we will provide audit logs (read/write events), a signed attestation from our security team, and export hashes for verification.
4) Escrow/hand-off: we create an immutable snapshot and coordinate SFTP/secure transfer; Redwood will schedule purge actions once MediFlow confirms successful ingest and verification.
5) Exceptions: any extension beyond 30 days or additional subprocessor retention must be documented in a DPA addendum.

Kimberly / Karthik — can you confirm the minimum clause language and whether 30 days is feasible without escalated sign-off?

Sara — attaching a draft subprocessor transfer checklist to make the ops flow explicit. If this looks acceptable I'll loop in Legal and Ops for final DPA language and a DocuSign path.

Best,
Aditya
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Temporal archival escape hatch - need confirmation

Thanks Aditya — looping Legal and Data Lifecycle to propose concrete language.

Draft clause (high level):
"During a discrete subprocessor migration, Redwood may retain ephemeral operational logs and immutable snapshots for the sole purpose of transfer validation and forensic analysis for a period not to exceed thirty (30) calendar days, unless Customer and Redwood agree in writing to an extension. Redwood will maintain access logs and provide a signed attestation describing the snapshots transferred, export hashes, and a timeline of purge actions. All retained artifacts shall be securely destroyed upon completion of the validation window."

Requirements / checklist for MediFlow prior to retention:
- Written migration start and end dates
- Point of contact for verification and acceptance
- Confirmation of target subprocessor and transfer mechanism (SFTP / provider)
- NDA or Data Processing Addendum signed with explicit addendum (we can draft)

Operational constraints: 30 days is acceptable with our standard addendum; any request >30 days will require GC approval and an internal risk review. We will require MediFlow to accept a limited attestation that Redwood performed only the transfer/validation actions described.

I'll draft the DPA addendum and send for review; Aditya please confirm you want DocuSign once we have signatures.

-Kim
Kimberly Park

Redwood Inference

Aditya / Kim — this looks good, thanks.

Two quick asks before we execute:
- Can Redwood confirm the purge action is a one-way action with verifiable deletion (not just logical unlink)? We need evidence (delete logs + snapshot hash mismatch confirmation).
- Please include a short timeline template in the DPA addendum indicating dates for snapshot creation, transfer window, verification window, and purge action.

We are okay with the 30-day default; if we need an extension we'll submit a formal request. Please send the DPA addendum and I will get the signatures from our side. We prefer DocuSign.

Onward — Sara
